title: As a developer, I can build a working phone voice agent — prompt, voice, and phone number — and take my first live call within an hour
As a founder, I can design multi-step conversation flows in a visual builder with branching, states, and handoffs without writing code
As a developer, I can run conversations in multiple languages, including detecting and switching language mid-call
As a developer, I can inject dynamic variables and per-caller context at call time so each conversation is personalized
As a developer, I can ground the agent on my documents with a built-in knowledge base or RAG so it answers from my content
As a platform-engineer, I can see documented end-to-end voice latency numbers or tuning guidance backing the platform's speed claims
As a developer, I can rely on the agent to handle interruptions (barge-in) gracefully — stopping speech, updating context, and recovering the turn
As a developer, I can use model-based end-of-turn detection beyond simple VAD silence timeouts so the agent doesn't talk over slow speakers
As a developer, I can enable noise suppression or audio filtering so the agent stays coherent on noisy real-world calls
As a developer, I can provision phone numbers and run both inbound and outbound calls through the platform's API
As a platform-engineer, I can connect my own carrier or PBX via SIP trunking (or import Twilio/Telnyx numbers) instead of being locked to bundled telephony
As a developer, I can escalate a live call to a human with warm or blind transfer, passing context along
As a developer, my agent can send DTMF keypresses, navigate IVR menus, and detect or leave voicemail
As a founder, I can run batch outbound call campaigns with scheduling and throughput controls
As a developer, my agent can call external APIs and custom functions mid-conversation and speak the result without awkward dead air
As an AI-native user, my voice agent can plug in MCP servers as tool sources so one integration grants it whole toolsets mid-call
As a developer, I can extract structured data from every call — outcomes, entities, dispositions — delivered via API or webhook after the call
As a developer, I can choose from a broad voice library or plug in multiple TTS providers to get the voice I want
As a founder, I can clone a custom brand voice and use it for my agents, with a documented consent process
As a developer, I can get accurate real-time transcription with control over the STT provider, language models, or key terms
As a platform-engineer, I can retrieve full call recordings and transcripts programmatically for every call
As a developer, I can test agents with simulated conversations or evals before putting them on real phone calls
As a founder, I can see call analytics — success rates, durations, outcomes, sentiment — in dashboards without building my own
As an AI-native user, the platform's AI reviews my calls for me — scoring quality, flagging failures, and analyzing resolution automatically
As a platform-engineer, I can monitor live calls in production and get alerts when agents misbehave or error rates spike
As a founder, I can meet call-recording consent and disclosure obligations with per-call recording controls and configurable data retention
As a platform-engineer, I can run regulated workloads with HIPAA/BAA support, SOC 2, and data-residency options
As a platform-engineer, I can self-host the voice agent runtime from open-source code on my own infrastructure
As a platform-engineer, I can see documented concurrency limits and scale to many simultaneous calls without manual capacity begging
As a founder, I can see published per-minute or usage pricing and estimate cost per call before committing

As an AI-native user, my coding agent can provision a complete voice agent end to end — create the agent, attach a number, and place a call — through the API, CLI, or MCP without touching the dashboard
As an AI-native user, the platform's own AI helps me author agents — generating or improving prompts, flows, and test cases from a description
